sources: Penn State Extension, Multicolored Asian Lady Beetle: first established US populations found in Louisiana in 1988; tens of thousands can congregate in attics, ceilings and wall voids; gather on south or southwest-facing sides on sunny afternoons after cold nights; when disturbed they exude a stinky yellow defensive chemical from their leg joints that can spot walls; they occasionally bite people; a black W on the white pronotum; vacuum with a nylon stocking in the hose; https://extension.psu.edu/multicolored-asian-lady-beetle

beats.say: Tens of thousands of beetles can be packed inside your walls.
Bug one, and it leaks stinky, yellow goo, right from its knees.
It's not a ladybug. Look for the black W, behind its head.
And sometimes? It even bites you.
